trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning to rest on board or prepare for landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€6.75 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to Eixample. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Gaudí's Casa Batlló, Domènech i Montaner's Casa Lleó Morera, and Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Amatller from the outside for free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Eixample neighbourhood on foot as the heat eases. Stroll down Carrer del Consell de Cent and enjoy the modernist architecture lit up at dusk. Grab a casual dinner nearby and get an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport for under €4.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (filled baguette) from a local bakery or Mercadona supermarket near the hotel for €2–4 — a great budget first meal.
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament) — a beloved local bar in nearby Sant Antoni with affordable tapas (patatas bravas, croquetas) for €10–14 per person including a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) on arrival — it covers all metro and bus journeys and will save money throughout the trip. August is peak season; stay hydrated and carry a refillable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with Gaudí's masterpiece — La Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance (€26 basic entry, or €36 with tower access — book the tower for the architectural detail). Arrive at opening time (9:00) to beat crowds. Spend 2–2.5 hours marvelling at the facades, the forest-like interior columns, and the stained glass light show.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (€10 entry for the Monumental Zone — book online). Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the serpentine bench with panoramic views over Barcelona. The surrounding free park areas are equally beautiful and worth exploring. Afterwards, descend through the Gràcia neighbourhood and browse its charming squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born district for the evening. Walk through the medieval streets and admire the Gothic architecture around Santa Maria del Mar basilica (free entry or small donation). Join the local nightlife scene — El Born has dozens of atmospheric bars. Start with vermouth at Bar del Pla, then bar-hop along Carrer del Rec.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area or a neighbourhood café near the hotel — café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a toast with tomato for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or in Gràcia — 3 courses with bread and drink for €12–14. Look for handwritten chalkboard signs outside restaurants.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada, El Born) — an iconic old-school bar serving house cava and tapas. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book both Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online to avoid sellouts and skip queues — this is essential in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes; today involves significant uphill walking at Park Güell.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — one of Europe's best-preserved medieval city centres and completely free to explore. Wander through narrow labyrinthine streets, find the Roman temple ruins of Temple d'August (free), and admire the Barcelona Cathedral exterior. Get pleasantly lost — every alley reveals something new.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to La Barceloneta beach (free) for an afternoon swim and sunbathing — a 20-minute walk from the Gothic Quarter or quick metro ride. Afterwards, walk along the Port Olímpic waterfront and up to the striking Frank Gehry Fish sculpture. Explore the colourful Barceloneta neighbourhood streets. Optional: visit the free Barceloneta Market building for a cool architectural break.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife. Pre-drink with affordable beers or sangria at a bar in El Raval (try Bar Marsella, one of Barcelona's oldest bars, or Kentucky Bar). Then head to one of the free-entry clubs in the Port Olímpic area or catch live music at a jazz bar in El Born. Clubs typically don't fill up until 1:00–2:00 AM.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament) — popular brunch spot with avocado toast and good coffee for €8–11, or grab pastries from La Boqueria's edge stalls for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach! Buy supplies from a Mercadona or Lidl supermarket — bread, cheese, cured meats, fruit, and a drink for €5–7 total.
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada (Barceloneta) — legendary local spot, cash only, no reservations. Try the bombas (their invention!) and grilled fish. Arrive early as it closes when food runs out. Budget €10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter and Barceloneta — pickpocketing is common in tourist-heavy areas. Use a crossbody bag or money belt. Nightlife in Barcelona starts very late; a nap in the afternoon is a local tradition (and a budget traveller's best friend).

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Montjuïc and ride the cable car or funicular (covered by T-Casual card) up to the hill. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for sweeping panoramic views of the city, port, and coastline. Explore the castle's history and ramparts. Then walk down through the beautiful Jardins de Laribal (free) — terraced gardens with fountains perfect for a cool morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Montjuïc's Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) — one of Spain's finest modern art museums, showcasing the colourful, surrealist works of Barcelona-born Miró. The building itself, designed by Josep Lluís Sert, is an architectural highlight. Alternatively, the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (€10) is a must for architecture lovers — a minimalist icon of 20th-century design. Head back to Eixample and explore the Modernisme Route — many building facades are free to admire.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Sant Antoni neighbourhood (a 10-minute walk from your hotel) — one of Barcelona's hippest areas that locals love. Browse the Sant Antoni Market building (beautifully restored Modernista structure). Enjoy pre-dinner vermouth at one of the terraces, then bar-hop along Carrer del Parlament and Carrer de Manso for craft cocktails and a lively local crowd.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader (Carrer d'en Xuclà, near Raval) — a historic milk bar open since 1870. Try the suís (hot chocolate with cream) and a pastry for €5–7.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (Carrer de Mallorca, Eixample) — famous for pintxos and tapas. Go at opening (1:00 PM) to avoid queues. Budget €13–17 per person.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda, Sant Antoni) — a no-frills neighbourhood bodega with excellent house wine (€2/glass) and simple, delicious tapas. Budget €10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Fundació Joan Miró offers free entry on Saturday afternoons after 15:00 — check the current schedule to save €14. Montjuïc gets very hot in August; go early and carry water. The funicular from Paral·lel metro station is the easiest and cheapest way up.

day_by_day.morning: Visit La Boqueria Market (Mercat de Sant Josep) on La Rambla — arrive before 10:00 to beat the tourist rush and see it as locals do. Browse the stunning stalls of fresh produce, seafood, meats, and spices. Buy fresh fruit or a small snack. Then walk the full length of La Rambla down to the Columbus Monument (free exterior viewing) and the waterfront for a final look at the port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Eixample for some last-minute architecture hunting — seek out lesser-known Modernista gems like Casa Comalat (Carrer de Còrsega), Casa Lleó i Morera details, and the stunning lamp posts and hexagonal pavement tiles (designed by Gaudí) along Passeig de Gràcia. Visit the free courtyard of Casa Lleó Morera if open. Do any last souvenir shopping at the Encants Vells flea market (open Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat) or pick up affordable gifts at local shops rather than tourist traps on La Rambla.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final sunset drink on a rooftop terrace — La Isabela rooftop at the Almanac Hotel or the more budget-friendly Bar Calders terrace. Have a farewell dinner in the neighbourhood, then pack and prepare for departure. Reflect on five incredible days of Modernista architecture, vibrant nightlife, and authentic Barcelona culture.

meals.breakfast: Bar Kasparo (Plaça de Vicenç Martorell, Raval) — a beloved local café with outdoor seating, great coffee, and fresh juices for €4–7.
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local Eixample restaurant — your last chance for a full 3-course Spanish lunch for €12–14. Look for spots filled with office workers (a reliable quality indicator).
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza (Carrer de de Londres) — beloved local pizzeria with creative toppings, natural wines, and a cool vibe. Large pizzas €13–16, perfect for a relaxed final evening. Or return to a favourite spot from earlier in the trip.

day_by_day.notes: If flying out on the 19th, confirm departure time and factor in 2–3 hours for airport travel and check-in. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya takes 35 minutes to the airport. Keep €10–15 in cash for the journey. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights): €350–450 per person, covering accommodation, transport, entry fees, and meals at the prices suggested.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Take the Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud from El Prat Airport to central Barcelona (~35 min, €5-6). Head directly to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample to check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Architecture Stroll: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia — the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) showcases Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera side by side. Admire the facades and consider a quick visit inside Casa Batlló (€29-35). This is walkable from your hotel and perfect for easing into the city.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner & First Taste of Eixample Nightlife: Explore the Eixample Esquerra neighbourhood, known locally as 'Gayxample', with a lively bar scene. Start dinner early (Spanish style around 21:00) then enjoy a cocktail at one of the stylish rooftop bars or terrace bars on Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or on arrival — try a café con leche and tostada con tomate at a local bar near the hotel (€3-5)
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — beloved local spot for tapas and montaditos, expect €15-20 per person
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda — a charming neighbourhood wine bar and restaurant in Eixample serving Catalan classics like escalivada and croquetes, around €25-35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 13:00, keep Day 1 relaxed and local. Avoid booking any timed-entry tickets for this afternoon. Purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport for the week — it will save money on transport across all days.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Book the first or second morning slot (9:00 or 10:00) to beat the August crowds. The skip-the-line guided tour (~1.5-2 hrs) reveals Gaudí's symbolic use of light, nature, and geometry in breathtaking detail. Climb the towers for panoramic views over Eixample. The basilica is a 15-minute walk or short metro ride from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration: Take the Metro or a 20-minute walk uphill to Park Güell. Explore the UNESCO-listed monumental zone with its iconic mosaic dragon staircase and the Hypostyle Room (timed tickets ~€10, book in advance). Afterward, wander down into the bohemian Gràcia neighbourhood — browse its charming plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, full of local character.
day_by_day.evening: Gràcia Tapas Bar Hop & Evening: Gràcia has an excellent local bar scene away from tourist crowds. Enjoy a leisurely tapas crawl along Carrer de Verdi or around Plaça de la Virreina, then return to Eixample for a nightcap at one of the chic cocktail bars on Carrer d'Enric Granados (a pedestrianised boulevard with terraces).

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Josep bakery near Sagrada Família — fresh pastries, pa amb tomàquet, and coffee for €5-8
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia — creative montaditos and craft beer in a trendy setting, €12-18 per person
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Carrer de Londres — beloved Eixample spot with wood-fired Neapolitan pizza and natural wines, €20-28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book both Sagrada Família (skip-the-line guided) and Park Güell timed tickets online well in advance — August is peak season and both sell out days or weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for the uphill walk to Park Güell.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour: Take the Metro to Jaume I and join a guided Gothic Quarter walking tour (~2 hrs). Discover the Roman Temple of Augustus hidden inside a medieval courtyard, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and winding medieval lanes. The guided format reveals hidden history that's easy to miss solo.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market & El Born Food Tour: Walk from the Gothic Quarter to La Boqueria on La Rambla — sample fresh fruit, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, and seafood. Then continue into the El Born neighbourhood for the food tour portion: visit artisan shops, the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, stunning Gothic interior), and the El Born Cultural Centre with its excavated medieval ruins beneath a 19th-century iron market.
day_by_day.evening: El Born & Barceloneta Nightlife: El Born transforms at night into one of Barcelona's most atmospheric bar districts. Start with vermouth at a traditional bodega, then head to Barceloneta or the Port Olímpic area for a livelier late-night scene. Barcelona nightlife starts late — clubs and bars peak after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in El Raval (near Gothic Quarter) — excellent brunch spot with avocado toast and specialty coffee, €10-14
meals.lunch: Graze at La Boqueria stalls for a market lunch — fresh oysters, jamón, cheese, and a glass of cava for €15-20
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — legendary cava bar and tapas restaurant, famous for anchovies and house cava, €20-30 per person

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded in the morning — aim to arrive by 10:30 before the main tourist rush. Many stalls are priced for tourists; venture to the back of the market for more authentic and affordable options. El Born is compact and very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill & Architecture: Take the cable car or Bus Turístic to Montjuïc for panoramic city views. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14) — a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert housing Miró's colourful works. Explore the Jardins de Laribal terraced gardens and the Castell de Montjuïc for sweeping harbour views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Waterfront: Head down to Barceloneta beach for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. Walk the Passeig Marítim promenade and explore the Port Olímpic marina area. Visit the iconic Frank Gehry golden 'Fish' sculpture and the W Hotel's striking sail-shaped architecture along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Sunset & Nightlife on Passeig Marítim: Stay on the waterfront for the golden hour sunset over the Mediterranean — one of Barcelona's most memorable experiences. As the sun sets, the beach bars (chiringuitos) and clubs along Passeig Marítim come alive. This is the perfect evening for Barcelona's famous beach nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Cafè de l'Acadèmia near the Gothic Quarter or a local Eixample café — café con leche and tostada, €4-7
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta — legendary no-frills local restaurant, birthplace of the bombas (potato croquettes), cash only, €15-20 per person (arrive early, it closes when food runs out)
meals.dinner: Barraca on Passeig Marítim — upscale beachfront restaurant with excellent paella and seafood rice dishes, €30-45 per person (splurge-worthy for the setting)

day_by_day.notes: August sun in Barcelona is intense — bring sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, and stay hydrated on the beach. Barceloneta gets very crowded; arrive before 12:00 to secure a good spot. La Cova Fumada does not take reservations and has very limited hours — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & Sant Pere: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Lluís Domènech i Montaner's Art Nouveau masterpiece (guided tours ~€22, or attend a morning concert if available). The stained-glass ceiling and sculptural facade are among the most extraordinary architectural achievements in Europe. Located in the Sant Pere neighbourhood, just north of El Born.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poblenou & @22 Innovation District Architecture Walk: Take the Metro or a short taxi to Poblenou — Barcelona's former industrial district reinvented as a creative hub. Walk along Rambla del Poblenou (the local, authentic version of La Rambla), explore street art, and admire contemporary architecture including Jean Nouvel's Torre Agbar/Torre Glòries (the bullet-shaped tower). Visit the Palo Alto Market if it coincides (first weekend of the month). Browse design studios and concept stores.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Rooftop Cocktails in Eixample: Return to Eixample for a memorable farewell evening. Enjoy a rooftop cocktail at the Hotel Majestic or the Almanac Barcelona rooftop bar with views over Passeig de Gràcia. End the trip with a special dinner at a Catalan restaurant before a final stroll down the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia.

meals.breakfast: Alsur Café near El Born — excellent brunch with eggs, smashed avocado, and specialty coffee, €12-16
meals.lunch: Rambla del Poblenou tapas — try Bar Calders or a local neighbourhood restaurant for a menú del día (set lunch menu with starter, main, dessert, and wine) for €13-16 — excellent value
meals.dinner: Moments or Disfrutar for a splurge (€60-80+), OR Cervería Catalana for a mid-range farewell tapas spread (~€25-35) — both in Eixample, walkable from the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música Catalana tours in advance online — August slots fill up fast. If your departure flight is on Day 6 (August 20), pack bags the night before. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya to the airport runs every 5-10 minutes and takes ~35 minutes (€6.75 one way). Keep your T-Casual metro card for the airport journey if trips remain.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Allow time for baggage claim, private transfer, and hotel check-in at Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the iconic 'Block of Discord' — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Consider booking a premium ticket to enter Casa Batlló for a stunning immersive audio-visual experience of Gaudí's masterpiece.
day_by_day.evening: Begin your Barcelona nightlife initiation with cocktails at a rooftop bar in Eixample — Dry Martini or the rooftop of Hotel Majestic offer refined atmospheres with city views. Transition to dinner in the neighborhood before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a welcome amenity or light refreshment at the hotel upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca: a beloved Eixample institution serving outstanding tapas and pintxos. Arrive early to avoid a long wait or reserve ahead.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza (upscale Neapolitan-style) or Moments at Hotel Mandarin Oriental — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant delivering avant-garde Catalan cuisine just steps from Passeig de Gràcia.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance for a seamless luxury arrival. Ask the hotel concierge to pre-book Casa Batlló tickets and all subsequent experiences upon check-in. August in Barcelona is hot (28–34°C) — stay hydrated and carry sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Join a skip-the-line private or small-group guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Upgrade to include tower access for breathtaking elevated views of the city. The morning light filtering through the stained-glass windows on the Nativity façade side is extraordinary and best experienced early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Head to Gaudí's whimsical mosaic-tiled park for its iconic dragon staircase, the Hypostyle Room, and sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona. Afterwards, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood to wander its bohemian plazas, independent boutiques, and café terraces at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife scene. Start with pre-dinner drinks at El Nacional, a grand multi-concept gastronomic space in Eixample. Then explore the Eixample Esquerra (also known as 'Gayxample') bar scene or head to one of the district's sophisticated cocktail lounges before a late dinner — dining at 21:00–22:00 is perfectly normal in Barcelona.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Federal Café in Sant Antoni for specialty coffee, avocado toast, and artisan pastries — a 10-minute walk from Eixample.
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia — a beautifully decorated tapas bar near Park Güell serving creative montaditos and seasonal small plates in a stunning tiled interior.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants, this avant-garde dining experience by former elBulli chefs is a must for architecture and design lovers; the space itself is a work of art. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access separately as it sells out fast — the Nativity Tower offers a different perspective than the Passion Tower. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Park Güell's uneven mosaic paths. A taxi or Uber from Sagrada Família to Park Güell takes about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — Explore Barcelona's medieval heart with a premium private guide. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the Barcelona Cathedral, the Plaça Reial, hidden courtyards, and the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call). A private tour allows you to linger in the spots that captivate you most without being rushed.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market & El Born Food Tour — Transition from the Gothic Quarter into the adjacent El Born neighborhood. Begin with a curated visit to La Boqueria market to sample jamón ibérico, fresh seafood, local cheeses, and tropical fruits. Continue into El Born for a guided food and wine tour, stopping at artisan vermouth bars, pintxos spots, and the stunning Modernista iron-and-glass Mercat de Santa Caterina.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Sunset & Nightlife on Passeig Marítim — Head to Barceloneta Beach for the golden hour sunset over the Mediterranean. Enjoy champagne or cava at a premium chiringuito (beach bar). As night falls, the Passeig Marítim and Port Olímpic come alive — visit Shôko, Opium, or Pacha Barcelona for world-class DJ sets and a glamorous crowd.

meals.breakfast: Hofmann Pastisseria in El Born — one of Barcelona's finest pastry shops, celebrated for its buttery croissants and exquisite cakes. A short taxi ride from Eixample.
meals.lunch: During the El Born food tour, graze on high-quality tapas, pintxos, and market produce — a deliberately indulgent progressive lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Bestial — a sleek, design-forward Mediterranean restaurant with an outdoor terrace right on Barceloneta beach, offering fresh seafood and pasta with stunning sea views. Perfect for a pre-nightlife dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot — wear breathable clothing given August heat. La Boqueria can be very crowded mid-morning; the food tour guide will help you navigate strategically. For nightclubs, note that Barcelona's club scene starts very late (00:00–01:00) and peaks around 03:00.

day_by_day.morning: Architecture deep-dive day — Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana, a UNESCO World Heritage Modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Book a premium guided tour to access the ornate stained-glass ceiling and mosaic-encrusted stage. Afterwards, explore the nearby El Born neighborhood at leisure, visiting the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a stunning example of Catalan Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe — Take a private car or cable car to Montjuïc for a cultural afternoon. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion, Mies van der Rohe's iconic 1929 masterpiece of minimalist architecture — a pilgrimage site for architecture lovers. Explore the surrounding gardens and the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art in a building designed by Josep Lluís Sert.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop and cocktail bar circuit in Eixample — Begin at the rooftop bar of Hotel Casa Fuster (a Modernista landmark) for sunset cocktails, then move to Bar Calders in Sant Antoni for a local aperitivo atmosphere. End the evening at a late-night jazz club such as Jamboree in Plaça Reial for live music and a sophisticated nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Cosmo on Carrer d'Enric Granados — a stylish café on one of Barcelona's most beautiful pedestrian boulevards, lined with Modernista buildings. Order eggs Benedict and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Tickets — the playful tapas bar by the Adrià brothers (elBulli legacy). Reservations open 60 days in advance online and are highly competitive; secure this well ahead. Located near Montjuïc, perfectly timed for the afternoon visit.
meals.dinner: Alkimia in Eixample — a one-Michelin-starred restaurant offering a refined tasting menu of reimagined Catalan classics in an elegant, intimate setting just minutes from the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: The Palau de la Música Catalana also hosts evening concerts — check the August program and consider booking tickets for a live performance as an alternative evening activity. The Barcelona Pavilion is closed on Mondays; confirm opening hours in advance. Montjuïc cable car offers spectacular views but runs on a schedule — check timings.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Eixample — Stroll along the elegant Enric Granados pedestrian boulevard, often called Barcelona's Champs-Élysées, lined with Modernista buildings, café terraces, and design boutiques. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies — a converted Modernista publishing house turned contemporary art museum — for a final dose of architecture and culture before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping on Passeig de Gràcia — Browse flagship stores and Spanish designer boutiques. Pick up premium local gifts: artisan chocolate from Enric Rovira, cava from a specialist wine shop, or a custom item from a Catalan design studio. Return to hotel for checkout and arrange a private luxury transfer to Barcelona El Prat Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — allow ample time for the airport transfer (30–45 minutes from Eixample depending on traffic). If the flight departs late evening, consider a final dinner at the airport's VIP lounge or a quick farewell meal at a nearby Eixample restaurant before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the hotel or at Forn de Sant Jaume on Rambla de Catalunya — a historic Eixample bakery serving exceptional pastries, pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato), and coffee.
meals.lunch: Bar Mut on Carrer de Pau Claris — a sophisticated Eixample brasserie with a beautiful Modernista interior, serving refined Catalan dishes and an excellent wine list. Ideal for a relaxed final lunch.
meals.dinner: If departing late: a farewell dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda — a charming wine bar and restaurant in Eixample offering natural wines and seasonal Catalan small plates in an intimate, candlelit setting.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed to maximize your final morning. Pre-book the airport transfer to avoid last-minute stress. Consider asking the hotel concierge to arrange a surprise farewell amenity — champagne, flowers, or a curated gift box of local products — as a memento of the trip.
